newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CEZ SHARES FALL SHARPLY, REBOUND SEEN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CEZ SHARES FALL SHARPLY, REBOUND SEEN.

text.p: Shares in Czech power utility CEZ a.s. fell sharply in early trading on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) on Friday but dealers said there was firm support at the current price and expected a rebound later in the session.
Just after the start of continuous trading CEZ was down 40 crowns, 3.2 percent, to 1,200.
"Before the fixing there was a big fall but it seems that CEZ has very good support at 1,200 crowns," said Lubomir Vystavel from ING Barings.

CEZ, the second most heavily capitalised share on the PX50 index, has long trailed other major issues because of investor worries about state regulated energy prices. At the same time it is seen as a cheap way to get into Czech blue chip issues.
Since the beginning of the year, it has been one of the star performers on the PSE rising by more than 14 percent in the last month alone.
Vystavel said Friday's decline was probably caused by a small number of sales and saw no reason why CEZ should not regain ground as the session progressed.
